payload.acceptance_criteria:
When quality-gates runs on main, every check runs and the workflow finishes within 15 minutes.
When any pytest shard fails, the quality workflow fails and names the failing test.
payload.description:
## Context
When a release or a fix is pushed, I want the quality workflow to finish in about ten minutes, so a one-line change does not cost an hour of CI.

## Finding
2026-11-16: quality-gates 43950875696 on c6b93711 was cancelled by timeout-minutes: 30. pytest passed (9537 passed in 25:45) and the job was cut off in pytest-live-ledger. The last five quality runs took 29 to 30 minutes each. The same suite takes 7 to 8 minutes on the developer machine.

## Plan
Split pytest across about four parallel jobs (or shards), keep every check, and keep the release rule of a green run on the exact commit. A timeout raised to 45 minutes is a stopgap only; the split is the fix. Changes .github/workflows, so it needs owner approval. Not claimed and not built.
payload.title: Split the CI pytest run into parallel jobs so quality finishes in about ten minutes

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a blocker of an open record is closed as cancelled, blocked names that blocker and a remedy.
When blocked lists a record, it names at least one reason.
payload.description:
## Context
When a blocker is closed as cancelled, I want blocked to name it with a remedy, so a dependent is never blocked without a named reason.

## Finding
Reported by the dev session via the Orchestrator, 2026-11-17. Development ledger at acb2eea, session-start blocked table: 'dev-fj1.1 | open | dev-he2.1 (closed)' and 'dev-vbo | open | (empty) | 2'. The edges were removed by hand in development commit 4f580e3.

## Request
blocked names every closed-but-not-completed blocker with a remedy, and it never shows a blocked record without a named reason. Optionally, close --resolution cancelled lists the dependents it leaves blocked. Not claimed.
payload.title: A record closed as cancelled still blocks its dependents, and blocked does not say so

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a stop or session-end hook ends with events still queued in the clone, its output names the queued count, each queued id and the command that shares them.
When a stop or session-end hook shares every queued event, its output reports no queued events.
payload.description:
## Context
When a session ends with local events not shared to the vault, I want the stop hook to say so by name, so no queued event is hidden behind a success.

## Finding
2026-11-17, by code read during the 999 of 1000 diagnosis: .basicly/core/kit/tracker/vault_hooks.py:101-108. On stop and session-end, a LockUnavailableError becomes {deferred: another share in this clone is running and takes the queue}, and any _KEPT error, which includes ShareError (a ValueError) such as DeadlineError, becomes {skipped: ...} with exit 0. A share that ends at its 10 s deadline can leave events queued while every stop reports success. This breaks the 2026-11-13 rule that local events absent from the vault must be detected. Not yet proven to be the cause of the 999 of 1000 failure in quality-gates 43965947002.

## Fix
A stop that leaves events queued names them: the count, the ids and the command that shares them. Not claimed.
payload.title: Make a vault stop hook name the events it leaves queued instead of reporting a silent skip

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When eight sessions on two CPUs each write 125 comments to one clone, no write is refused for the pending view lock.
When a write is refused for a lock, its exit code is non-zero and its output names the lock.
payload.description:
## Context
When eight agent sessions write to one vault clone at once, I want each local write to be accepted quickly, so an agent swarm does not get refused writes it must retry.

## Finding
2026-11-17, probe of test_proof_t_agents_eight_sessions_in_three_worktrees_land_each_event_once on 2 CPUs (1 failure in 36 runs): 1 of 1000 comment writes exited 1 with {refused: another writer holds .../pending-r/.events.lock after 5.0s}. The refusal is safe and named, and the caller sees it. It caused the 999 of 1000 failure in quality-gates 43965947002 because the test agent ignored the exit code; the test now retries refused writes. Why a local write waits more than 5 s for the pending-view lock is not yet measured.

## Fix
Measure the pending-view lock hold time under 8 sessions and shorten the critical section, so a local write is not refused under that load. Not claimed.
payload.title: Keep a local vault write from waiting over five seconds for the pending view lock under eight sessions

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a consumer installs basicly, its projected guidance states the 5 and 10 minute CI budget.
When a consumer's normal CI run takes more than 5 minutes from push to green, the budget check fails and names the workflow and its time.
When a consumer's release CI run takes more than 10 minutes, the budget check fails and names the workflow and its time.
payload.description:
## Context
When a repository installs or upgrades basicly, I want it to inherit the CI time budget, so its normal CI stays within 5 minutes and its release CI within 10 minutes.

## Owner intent
2026-11-17, relayed by the Orchestrator in his words: "the same CI rule i have for basicly, CI max 5, release max 10 min must apply here, as it should be inherited when new version of basicly is installed in handily."

## Shape
A catalog rule that states the budget, plus a check that measures a consumer's CI wall time per workflow from push to green and fails when normal CI exceeds 5 minutes or release CI exceeds 10 minutes. Built in the CI phase after basicly-svtn4op. Not claimed.
payload.title: Make the CI time budget part of the harness that consumers inherit

payload.description:
## Context
When basicly finds a learning in a consumer repository, I want it to flow back to the main basicly repository with its evidence, so every installation improves the harness.

## Owner intent
2026-11-17, relayed by the Orchestrator in his words: "basicly must be able to learn and self-improve - if it is happening in a client repo, then it must know how to bring back the learning to the main basilcy repo, for example by creating a PR."

## Shape
To be shaped with the Orchestrator later: how a learning is recognised in a consumer, what evidence it carries, and how it returns, for example as a pull request to basicly. Not claimed.
payload.title: basicly learns and self-improves across repositories
